listings.name: Yangmingshan National Park
listings.content: A favourite destination, particularly during spring when thousands of calla lilies, peonies and cherry blossoms bloom in the valleys. Besides that public hot springs, as well as hot sulphur blow holes and sources are equally worth the visit. There are dozens of hiking trails in the park, most marked out on maps from the visitors centre. Qixingshan is the highest peak in Yangmingshan, and looks out over the Taipei Basin and the north coast.

listings.name: Golden Horse Chinese Language Film Festival
listings.content: Often referred to as the Oscars of the Chinese film world, while films in the awards section are all in Chinese, they have English subtitles and there is also a large non-competition foreign language section.

listings.name: Taipei Film Festival
listings.content: An international festival with two award sections – Taipei Award Nominees and International New Talent Nominees. Films are shown at several venues throughout the city.

listings.name: Beitou Hot Springs Museum
listings.content: Built during the Japanese occupation, this beautiful Euro-Japanese style building was once the main public bath in Beitou. It has been lovingly restored and was re-opened in its current form in 1998. Through the twelve rooms, the story of Beitou's romantic years of steam and mystery are revealed in interesting displays.

listings.name: Ketagalan Cultural Center
listings.content: This ten-story building is dedicated to the Aboriginal culture that once flourished in the Beitou area.

listings.name: Kuandu Museum of Fine Arts
listings.content: an art museum on Taipei National University of the art.

listings.name: Beitou Park
listings.content: A long, narrow park. Within the park are fountains, the Beitou library, the Beitou Hot Springs Museum and an outdoor hot spring. Due to its central location, the park is a useful landmark for locating Beitou's other attractions. The park is also featured in the Hong Kong movie Turn Left, Turn Right, starring with Takeshi Kaneshiro and Gigi Leung.

listings.name: Geothermal Valley
listings.content: This is one of the most famous spots in Beitou, a natural sulfur hot spring where water temperatures can reach 100°C (212°F).

listings.name: Millennium Hot Spring
listings.content: An outdoor public mixed-gender hot spring. A great choice for the budget minded. Swimwear is required; you can purchase it on-the-spot, but choices are limited and somewhat expensive. They have a number of rules, available on English signs; it would behoove you to follow them lest the guy in the red shirt blow his whistle at you.

listings.name: Emperor Spa
listings.content: Traditional Japanese-style sex-segregated nude hot spring. Entry is free if you spend at least $400 at their restaurant; the seafood porridge is particularly famous. Private spa rooms are also available. Both this and neighboring Kawayu Spa have a reputation for being gay cruising spots.

listings.name: Amalfi
listings.content: A cozy Italian vegetarian restaurant. Excellent pizza. Friendly and fast service. Coffee/tea.

listings.name: Shanxi Beef Noodles
listings.content: A small noodle shop that serves beef with hand-cut noodles in tomato broth and other simple delicious meals.

listings.name: Yummy Vegan Home
listings.content: Delicious vegan cuisine. Burgers, pasta, hummus, healthy drinks. Bright and pleasant interior. English menu.

listings.name: N Cafe
listings.content: Excellent coffee. Innovative cafe cuisine.

listings.name: On My Way．Taipei Hostel
listings.content: A cozy and clean hostel with good facilities. Staff very helpful and interested in their work.

listings.name: Beauty Age Hotel
listings.content: This hotel offers a very relaxing and pleasant environment.
listings.price: Double rooms from NT$1,920 (NT$2,560 at weekends) to NT$3,150 (NT$4,200 at weekends)

listings.name: Radium Kagaya
listings.content: Official Taiwanese branch of the famed Kagaya hot spring hotel in Wakura Onsen, Japan. Japanese-style ryokan with superlative Japanese-style service, Japanese-style meals and prices to match. Day use of the public baths is also available ($1200) but many visitors opt for the private spa rooms instead.

listings.name: Spring City Resort
listings.content: A five star hot springs resort overlooking the Beitou valley.

listings.name: Sweetme Hot Spring Resort
listings.content: Despite the hotel's rather uninspiring English name, the resort offers a pleasant environment to relax and unwind, and is conveniently located within a two minute walk from Xin Beitou MRT Station.

listings.name: Longshan Temple
listings.content: This temple is where countless generations of Taipei citizens have come to pray and seek guidance at times of trouble. As the temple is dedicated to Guanyin (the Buddhist representation of compassion) it is officially defined as Buddhist, but there is a great amount of folk religion mixed into the fabric of the beliefs at this temple.
listings.address: No.211, Guangzhou Rd, Wanhua Dist. (near junction with Guilin Road)

listings.name: Red House
listings.content: Near the Ximending shopping area, the Red House was Taiwan's first modern market as well as a theater. Now, the renovated structure is home to an exhibition hall and a market selling innovative handicrafts.

listings.name: North Gate
listings.content: Of the five ancient city gates, four are still standing. But of the four, only one is a true historical relic from the Qing Dynasty: the salmon-colored north gate, whose formal name in Cheng'en Gate (承恩門). It was built in a traditional South Fujian architectural style. Its external walls were built with granolithic and brown mosaic tiles from Beitou Kiln.

listings.name: Bopiliao Old Street
listings.content: One of the few, and probably best preserved, examples of Qing dynasty architecture in Taipei. The street features historic red brick buildings which have been well restored and are used for a variety of cultural purposes.

listings.name: Beimen Metro Station
listings.content: Displays some archeological remains from the Qing Dynasty. Arguably not worth a detour, but keep your eyes peeled when changing trains.

listings.name: Huaxi Street Night Market
listings.content: This area had long been Taipei's most notorious red-light district, filled with brothels, pornography shops and snake meat restaurants in which the snakes would be killed and skinned in the street to attract potential customers. However, prostitution was banned by the Taiwanese government 1991 and the area has been thoroughly gentrified, with the last snake meat restaurant closing down in 2018. Today, it is just a regular family-friendly night market with the usual Taiwanese street food.

listings.name: Dadaocheng Presbyterian Church
listings.content: The architectural design of this church represents a fusion between traditional Chinese and late 19th-century Western style architecture. It maintains a unique position in the modern architecture of Taiwan, being one of only three extant Presbyterian churches in Taipei built during the Japanese occupation period. Historically, men would enter and exit through the left door, and women would enter and exit through the right door.

listings.name: Gui-de Street
listings.content: Previously called Western Houses Street, this lane once fronted the Danshui River. In the 1880s, the world famous Formosa Oolong Tea came from a nearby wharf. At the time, many wealthy merchants invested in building along the lane in order to attract international trading firms. One was Chen Tian-lai (AD 1872-1939), a Taiwanese tea merchant, who was fabulously rich for his time. His home was one of the model Taiwanese residences on this land and his neo-Baroque home is still standing. (No.73 Gui-De Street)
listings.address: West of Dihua Street and Xining North Road

listings.name: Museum of Contemporary Art
listings.content: MOCA Taipei is Taiwan's first art space dedicated to contemporary work. The red brick building was erected by the Japanese in 1921 and formerly served as Taipei City Hall as well as an elemantary school.

listings.name: Sin Hong Choon
listings.content: A former tea factory and storefront built in 1934 with blended east-west architecture, now a museum on the history of Taipei tea markets and Taiwanese tea production. The upstairs cafe offers introductory tea tastings.
listings.address: No. 309號, Minsheng W Rd, Datong District

listings.name: Ama Museum
listings.content: The museum is dedicated to the comfort women during the Japanese rule of Taiwan.
listings.address: No.32, Sec. 3, Chengde Rd, Datong Dist

listings.name: Dalongdong Baoan Temple
listings.content: Construction began on this temple in 1805 and was completed 25 years later. Baoan is a Taoist temple and one of the leading religious sites in Taipei. The temple's main deity is the emperor Baosheng, the god of medicine. The mural paintings and sculptures that adorn the building are considered some of the most impressive in Taiwan, and the temple won acclaim in the 2003 UNESCO Asia-Pacific Heritage Awards.

listings.name: Taipei Confucius Temple
listings.content: Just next to Bao'an Temple, the Confucius Temple was built in 1879 when the Qing Court changed Taipei into a prefecture of the Province of Fujian, China. It was established to serve as the largest educational center in northern Taiwan. Every September 28, a large number of people from Taiwan and abroad come here to watch a solemn Confucius birthday ceremony and eight-row dance.

listings.name: Chen Dexing Ancestral Hall
listings.content: An ancestral shrine built in 1892

listings.name: Fa-Chu-Kung Temple
listings.content: A 5-storey temple building built in 1878.

listings.name: Xiahai City God Temple
listings.content: This historic Taoist temple was built in 1859 to worship Xiahai, the City God (城隍爺), who watched over the citizens in the district and decided a person's fate after death. It might be small, with an area of only about 46 square meters, but it one of Taipei's most important places of worship, and is the area's religious and social center. In addition to Xiahai, this temple is dedicated to 600 gods, including his wife, the old man under the moon, the Eight Officials, civil and military judges, General Fan Xie (seven masters and eight masters), the Eight Generals, Ma Shiye and Yiyong Gong.

listings.name: Machangding Memorial Park
listings.content: The park features an artificial mound on the approximate site where a number of people were executed during the period of marshal law. The park is dedicated to those who lost their lives during this period.

listings.name: Ah Chung Mee Soa
listings.content: You can't miss this shop in Ximending, since crowds of people surround it all day. Standing or sitting, they slurp down hot bowls of mee soa, which are a comfort on cold days. Not quite for the faint-hearted, thin noodles are mixed with a flavorful soup, created from prolonged braising of the (thoroughly washed) large intestines of the pig. Don't forget to add the condiments provided at the side: the vinegar and minced garlic packs a punch. Other branches can be found in Shilin Night Market and Zhongxiao Fuxing.

listings.name: Calcutta Indian Curry House
listings.content: Basement Level of the Wannian Shopping Complex, Ximending - One of the more popular Indian restaurants. A bit hard to find, but definitely worth it.

listings.name: Qiaotou Sushi
listings.content: A traditional Taiwanese-style sushi establishment. Although the environs are rather average, the location is rather spacious. NT$25 will get you a big bowl of miso soup with tofu, which goes well with a serving of cold sushi. The sashimi sushi is also worth trying for NT$140, also with decent portion sizes.

listings.name: The Clover
listings.content: A small number of vegetarian meals set a Nt$99. Homemade sauces. Simple and clean interior. Fast service.

listings.name: Mei Guan Yuan
listings.content: Located in Ximending Pedestrian Area. This restaurant has served authentic Japanese sushi and sashimi since 1946. (There's another restaurant opposite the road from this with exactly the same name - that's the old location of this restaurant and doesn't serve as good sushi.)

listings.name: Liu Yu Teahouse
listings.content: An unpretentious and cozy tea house. Excellent selection of teas. Owner speaks fluent English.
listings.address: B1-10, Longshan Temple Underpass, No145 Xiyuan Road. Sec. 1, Wanhua

listings.name: Somebody Cafe
listings.content: Hang out place for artists. A quiet space among the neon and bustle of the area. Cozy interior with lots of plants. Tasty, simple meals. Excellent coffee.

listings.name: Backpacker Hostel
listings.content: Clean. Cafe style communal area. Private and dorm rooms.

listings.name: Dan Hostel
listings.content: Modern hostel with an industrial vibe. Stylish communal area. Single, twin, and dorm rooms. Two minute walk from Ximen metro station.

listings.name: Wow Hostel
listings.content: Dorms and private rooms. Compacted, but comfortable spaces. Clean and well-maintained communal area.

listings.name: CU Hotel Taipei
listings.content: Next to the Ningxia Night Market, this hotel is a stone's throw away from the Shuanglian MRT station, and is geared towards both business and leisure travelers.

listings.name: Fortune Hiya Hotel
listings.content: Good location and staff. Convenient to transportation, shopping, and dining.

listings.name: Yi Su Hotel
listings.content: Near the Ningxia Night Market. Rooms and bathrooms are rather small, though.

listings.name: Palais de Chine Hotel
listings.content: 5-star top-notch accommodation, offering a comfortable and aesthetic environment as well as personalized, attentive services.

listings.name: Taipei World Trade Center Nangang Exhibition Hall
listings.content: Taipei’s trade-show venue.

listings.name: Academia Sinica
listings.content: Home to several research institutions, such as the Genomic Research Center, the Institute of Biomedical Sciences, and the Institute of Cellular and Organismic Biology.

listings.name: Guo Ziyi Memorial Hall
listings.content: A Japanese-era building, built in a baroque architectural style, that exhibits various documents on Tang Dynasty poets, calligraphy and paintings.

listings.name: Tomb of Dong Zuobin
listings.content: The tomb of Dong Zuobin, a famous Chinese archeologist

listings.name: Tomb of Hu Shih
listings.content: The tomb of Hu Shih, famous philosopher, essayist, and diplomat who was influential on the May Fourth Movement that toppled the Qing dynasty in China.

listings.name: Hu Shih Memorial Hall
listings.content: A small museum dedicated to the archeologist Hu Shih which contains a number of artifacts related to ancient Chinese history. There is an audio guide available in English.

listings.name: Lingnan Fine Arts Museum
listings.content: The museums features the first professional archive of Lingnan paintings in Taiwan.

listings.name: Bishan Temple
listings.content: The largest Taoist temple in Neihu. It offers spectacular views of Taipei on a clear day. It is possible to spend the night here by offering a donation. There are other interesting Buddhist and Taoist temples nearby. Ride the local Red 2 bus to the Temple. Attractions include a golden statue and beautiful architecture. Walk down from the temple to the city for addition appreciation of the flora of Taiwan.

listings.name: Dahu Park
listings.content: A popular area for recreation. It boasts a large lake with a famous Chinese-style arched bridge. There complementing the lake is a lakeside swimming pool and Egret Mountain which is adjacent to the lake a great hiking location. The swimming pool is a little outdated and in needs some refurnishing, but it's only NT$110 for a swim which includes access to the jacuzzi, steam room, sauna and the high-powered water jets that regulars use to relieve stress from their tired and aching muscles. There's also a freezing cold plunge pool for those without a faint heart. There is a 25 m indoor pool, a 50 m outdoor pool and a kids' pool with a climbing apparatus and water jets to play with. Since it's right next to Dahu park so once you've had a swim you can enjoy the park's facilities including a foot massage path and basic exercise equipment. It's a great place for exercising.

listings.name: Bihu Park
listings.content: A large park of 13 ha surrounding the Dapi lake.

listings.name: Nanhu Riverside Park
listings.content: A park that is bisected by the Keelung river which divides the two districts.

listings.name: Nangang Park
listings.content: A large district park that contains a u-shaped lake.

listings.name: Taipei Extreme Sports Training Center
listings.content: A sportsground for skateboarding and other more 'extreme' sports.

listings.name: Huo Guo Shi Jia
listings.content: Shabu Shabu restaurant behind the McDonalds by the mall next to Neihu Station. Good seafood and prices.

listings.name: Paradise Thai
listings.content: Best Thai place in town, better than Thai Town and Spice World. They have Taipei's only micro-brewry built into their restaurant. Great spicy Thai food and cold beer to wash it down. Prices are upper-end, but worth it.

listings.name: The Meeting Place
listings.content: A new hostel near Songshan Station and Houshanpi MRT, with a very large common area, free internet and guest computers, and other amenities.
listings.address: 1F, No. 20, Alley 1, Lane 768, Section 4, Bade Rd

listings.name: National Palace Museum
listings.content: Probably Taiwan's top sight, displaying the finest collection of treasures formerly owned by the Emperors of China. During the Sino-Japanese War, the Nationalist Government took artifacts from Beijing so they wouldn't be harmed by the invading Japanese. After the war ended, the Chinese Civil War continued and thus the Kuomintang shipped them to Taiwan. The Communists weren't very happy about this, but, as it turned out, transporting the imperial treasures to Taipei allowed them to escape the destruction that many historical artifacts suffered under the communists during the Cultural Revolution. The museum today houses what is quite possibly the best collection of Chinese art in the world. Its collection is so large that not all of it can be displayed at once, which means that exhibits change regularly. Its main highlights, known as the Three Treasures, are the Jadeite Cabbage (翠玉白菜 Cuìyù Báicài), the Meat-Shaped Stone (肉形石 ròuxíngshí) and the Mao Gong Ding (毛公鼎 Máogōng dǐng).
listings.price: NT$350 for adults, free for under 18s. NT$150 for students (with ISIC or Youth Travel card), and NT$320 per person for large groups (10 or more people)

listings.name: Taipei Astronomical Museum
listings.content: This modern museum offers a hands-on introduction to our universe. In addition to the permanent exhibits, there is also an Imax dome theater, an observatory and a 3D movie theater. Entrance to the observatory is free, while NT$100 (adult) NT$50 (child) is charged for a show at each of the two theaters.

listings.name: Shung Ye Museum of Formosan Aborigines
listings.content: This museum houses exhibitions of Aboriginal culture and lifestyle. An English audio guide is available.

listings.name: National Taiwan Science Education Center
listings.content: Science center with hands-on exhibits and bilingual displays.

listings.name: Shilin Residence
listings.content: It was one of Chiang Kai-shek's abodes during his Taipei years, and the sprawling grounds were opened as a park in 1996. This residence is famous for the European style of its architecture and gardens.

listings.name: Zhishanyan Cultural and Ecological Garden
listings.content: A small hill is in the south of Tianmu's Yangming Hospital, and north of the Shuangxi river. The Zhishan Hill (Zhishanyan 芝山岩), one of the oldest archaeological excavation sites in Taiwan. Along the trail, you can see many historic heritages in this hill, the Huiji Temple (惠濟宮), Fortified Gate, small temple and an old camphor tree over 300 years old. Getting there: MRT Zhishan Station (Danshui Line) and walk for about 15 minutes.

listings.name: Aborigine Culture Park
listings.content: The theme of the park is the aboriginal culture. There are sixteen stone-slab sculptures stand in the entrance of the park, depicting the people of Taiwan's sixteen tribes in their traditional costumes.

listings.name: Tianmu Shincong Cinema
listings.content: A very modern facility with eight screens.
listings.address: No.202, Zhongcheng Rd, 4F, sec 2, Tianmu (忠誠路二段202號4樓)

listings.name: Juice Meal Vegetarian Restaurant
listings.content: Dine-in service is no longer available; instead, vegetarian rice dumplings are available for takeaway.”
listings.address: No.34, Ln. 505, Sec. 5, Jhongshan N. Rd

listings.name: Jingxing Vegetarian Kitchen
listings.content: Simple, tasty Chinese vegetarian meals. Choose a set meal from the menu and it is served on a tray. Owner speaks English, and there's a picture menu in English and Chinese.

listings.name: Cafe Onion Restaurant
listings.content: Cafe Onion serves pastas and steaks. Tea or coffee are also available. Germany pork knuckles are good.

listings.name: Fangs Restaurant
listings.content: Popular amongst Taiwanese and expats, this 2-story restaurants offers excellent quality local dishes. There is an open kitchen where people can watch dumplings being made.

listings.name: Sanxitang Space
listings.content: Well-hidden slick teahouse/restaurant atop the Palace Museum, which looks more expensive than it is. Most people stop by for a pot of oolong and tiny pastries, but the menu (available in English) also covers dim sum and enough savouries to make a meal.

listings.name: Orange Cafe
listings.content: Pining for a cafe with a backstreet atmosphere and pumping out Indian, Middle Eastern, folk or Floyd type music? Check out Orange Cafe. In addition to coffee/tea etc, they also offer a simple menu that includes vegetarian dishes, and from 22:30 on Friday evening the place comes to life with a fire dance performance on the roof.

listings.name: Vagabond Cafe
listings.content: A spacious art-style cafe with large windows overlooking green space - documentary movies screened on Wednesdays and Saturdays at 19:30 - excellent coffee and home-made (including vegetarian) dishes.

listings.name: Play Taipei Backpackers
listings.content: This hostel offers full ensuite rooms with private bathrooms. There is no common area and no dorms. Clean, friendly staff.

listings.name: Fun Taipei @ Shilin Night Market
listings.content: A pleasant hostel with free wifi.

listings.name: Tango Inn
listings.content: A contemporary and stylish hotel. Excellent facilities. Efficient and friendly staff.

listings.name: The Maokong Gondola
listings.content: Runs from Taipei Zoo MRT station to Maokong, with stops at the Taipei Zoo South and Zhinan Temple stations. There are two types of cable cars - regular and crystal, which has a clear bottom. You have to select which type of car to board. There's no difference in ticket or price, only in waiting time. The line for the crystal cars takes much longer. However, it's not worth the wait as the view from the bottom of the crystal car is pretty much the same as the view you get from the sides of the regular car. Two bus lines serve the Maokong area: bus number S10, which departs from the Wanfang Community MRT Station, and bus number BR15, which can be boarded at the Taipei Zoo and Taipei City Hall MRT stations.
listings.price: NT$70/100/120 (1/2/3 station(s)), NT$20 off with EasyCard during weekdays

listings.name: Taipei Zoo
listings.content: Nestled in a tight, lush valley, Taipei zoo has all the leisurely charm of a large park, but you also get the enjoyment of wandering through trees and along lanes with a variety of animals and birds. Unlike many traditional zoos, the animals here are not confined to cages, but allowed to roam freely in open paddocks, and it is a very clean and well maintained facility. However, some of the animal enclosures are small and seem over-crowded. Due to the city government's education policy, the zoo is very much an integral part of Taipei life. So much so in fact, that when an old elephant became ill and died several years ago, several generations turned up, many with tears in their eyes, to say their farewells. The zoo is popular in Taiwan for its two pandas, a gift from China. The zoo is located in the suburb of Muzha, and the entrance is just outside the terminal stop on the Muzha MRT line, 'Taipei Zoo'. Admission is quite affordable, at NT$60 for adults, and if you have a Taipei Metro EasyCard, you can pay the admission fee with that.

listings.name: National Chengchi University
listings.content: NCCU, often abbreviated to Zhengda (政大), is Taiwan's leading national university focused on humanities and social sciences. It is large with lots of greenery and open spaces. There are hiking trails up the mountains in the back of the campus with teahouses and temples all over the hills. The campus grounds are surrounded by shops, bookstores, eateries, cafes and teahouses popular with students and scholars.

listings.name: Zhang Nai Miao Memorial Hall
listings.content: A small and intimate museum built in memory of tea master Zhang Nai Miao, who brought the first Tieguanyin plants from Anxi, Fujian to Zhanghu, Muzha, which marked the beginning of Tieguanyin tea cultivation in the area.

listings.name: Jingmei Jiying Temple
listings.content: Jingmei Jiying Temple honors Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan, both of whom fought and died bravely during the An Shi rebellion. It is one of Taiwan's designated historic monuments and a great example of Qing dynasty temple architecture.

listings.name: Zhinan Temple
listings.content: One of the most important of Taiwan's early Taoist temples, Zhinan Temple is dedicated to main deity Lu Dongbin, one of the Eight Immortals, and various other deities.

listings.name: Tian'en Temple
listings.content: A 4-storey Taoist temple dedicated to an eclectic mix of deities.

listings.name: Taipei Tea Promotion Center
listings.content: Offers introduction to tea picking, processing, brewing and free taste testing.

listings.name: Xianjiyan hiking trail
listings.content: Many curious visitors come here to see a footprint supposedly left by the Taoist deity Lu Dongbin. The view from Xianjiyan trail includes natural vistas as well as a bird's eye view of the southern districts of Taipei. Located on the hill behind Jingmei Night Market, this nicely built and well-marked network of trails also features a temple located along the trail. The main trails are all paved with concrete or raised wooden walkways, and are lit with lamps at night, so you can go for an evening walk or watch the sunset from the summit. There are no technically difficult trails, but be prepared to climb a long, steep stairway to get on top of the hill.

listings.name: Zhinan Temple & Cihui Temple hiking trail
listings.content: In addition to the beauty of the temples, visitors can also enjoy an excellent view of the Taipei Basin, Danshui River, and Guanyinshan.

listings.name: Zhangshan Temple hiking trail
listings.content: Offers spectacular views of the Taipei basin and Taipei 101 from in front of Zhangshan Temple.

listings.name: Ergeshan
listings.content: This is an excellent choice for a moderately strenuous hike lasting several hours. Ergeshan is the highest peak along a ridge trail extending from Shiding in the east to Ankeng in the West. The peak of Ergeshan is at the border of the Wenshan District and Taipei County. The hike to the ridge can be a challenge, but the ridge trail is excellent, offering spectacular views and the occasional glimpse of monkeys in the woods.

listings.name: Riverside Park
listings.content: Not a hiking trail, but popular among those out for a relaxed stroll. The various sections of the park run most of the length of Jingmei Stream, the main body of water in Wenshan District. The park is characterized by large grassy areas interspersed with public sports facilities (such as tennis courts and softball diamonds). It's a good place to go for casual exercise or for viewing the bird life around the creek (herons and egrets are a common sight).

listings.name: Fudekeng Environmental Restoration Park
listings.content: The park houses the first photovoltaic power station in Taipei.

listings.name: Muzha Park
listings.content: If you come at the right time of year, this is a good place to see fireflies.

listings.name: Dian Wei Chu Fang
listings.content: Offers delicious Yunnan style food.

listings.name: Tian Xiang Hui Wei
listings.content: Known for its Mongolian hotpot.

listings.name: Yao Yue Teahouse
listings.content: Offers creative tea cuisine with restful views over the surrounding countryside.

listings.name: Xing Hua Lin Teahouse
listings.content: Estimated best time for apricot blossom viewing - February to March. The best time for viewing varies according to the weather conditions.

listings.name: Taipei Visitors Hostel
listings.content: This hostel is more like a shared accommodation than a hostel. Visitors are able to choose the duration of their stay. The company has two locations and unlike normal hostels, all rooms are separate, each containing a double bed. Prices start at NT$3000 per week.

listings.name: Daan Forest Park
listings.content: The park rests on 26 hectares in central Taipei bordered by Xinyi Road, Jianguo South Road, Heping East Road, and Xinsheng South Road. Due to its size and location, it is also known as Taipei Central Park. Bus lines 15, 52, 235, 278, 284, 20, 22, Xinyi Main Line service this park.

listings.name: Discover Center Of Taipei
listings.content: Located just inside the main entrance of Taipei City Hall, this is a good place to know the history and culture of Taipei City.

listings.name: Songshan Cultural and Creative Park
listings.content: in 2011, the park turned into a full fledged art center. Now it is a hub for cultural activities and exhibits. You can walk around the park and see the old structures as well as the new exhibits, restaurants, and the Eslite mall. Within the Eslite mall you can participate in various activities including glass blowing, jewelry and soap making.
listings.address: No. 133, Guangfu South Road, Xinyi District

listings.name: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall
listings.content: Constructed in the memory of Dr. Sun Yat-sen who is the founding father of the Republic of China. The construction of the Memorial commenced in 1965 in conjunction with the 100th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth. It was opened on 16 May 1972, with the majestic architecture and placid landscape covering an area of some 115,500 m². The park named Zhongshan Park marks the front yard of the Hall. On the inside, there is a 19-foot bronze statue of Dr. Sun Yat-sen, watched over during the day by motionless military honor guards, along with a library of 400 seats storing over 1.4 million books. A changing of the guard ceremony is conducted every hour on the hour from 09:00 to 17:00, with a rifle twirling performance. The 100-m long Zhongshan corridor links the main hall to the four large exhibition buildings where contemporary arts and historical articles are frequently on display. The Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall has grown into much of a community center, and is much less touristy than the newer and larger Chiang Kai-shek Memorial. There is an auditorium which has weekly lectures and seminars on aspects of art and life. It is also a popular site for public concerts.

listings.name: Taipei 101
listings.content: (zh-TW 臺北國際金融大樓) is rich in symbolism. This 101-floor, 508-meter high skyscraper is designed to resemble bamboo rising from the earth, a plant recognized in Asian cultures for its fast growth and flexibility. The building is divided into eight distinct sections, with eight being a number associated with prosperity in Chinese culture. The internal architecture of Taipei 101 is similarly awe-inspiring. Pay attention to ornate details on the structural beams, columns, and other elements. It was the world's tallest building from 2004 to 2010, but was soon overtaken by others willing to splurge for bragging rights.

listings.name: Taipei 101 Indoor Observatory
listings.content: The world's second fastest elevators will zip visitors up to the 89th-floor observation deck in a mere 37 seconds. It's worth taking a ride up, as the views are stunning. The best time to visit would be in the late afternoon when you spend a couple of hours and see both day and night views of Taipei. Don't forget to look toward the middle of the Indoor Observatory, where you'll see the world's largest spherical tuned mass damper (one of three) that keeps the building steady during earthquakes. Also, it is probably best to come early (around 08:55) or you will have to stand in line for 15–60 min.
listings.price: NT$600 for adults, NT$370 for kids under 12

listings.name: Taipei 101 Outdoor Observatory
listings.content: You can also go up to the outdoor observatory on the 91st floor (while it's possible to go to the outdoor observatory in a wheelchair, the view is negligible, as the concrete railing is too high to see over). Often only the elevator side remains open and you cannot walk a circle—if this is important to you, ask ahead.

listings.name: Yongkang Street
listings.content: The lanes and alleys around Yongkang Street and Yongkang Park are packed with specialty restaurants, gift shops selling Taiwanese handicrafts, and distinctive cafes. A great place to spend a few hours strolling around.

listings.name: Taipei Grand Mosque
listings.content: The first and largest mosque in Taiwan.
listings.address: No. 62, Sec. 2, Xing Sheng South Road, Da'an District

listings.name: Elephant Mountain Hiking Trail
listings.content: A short walk from Taipei 101 in Xinyi District. Very steep steps lead up into a shaded, forested hill overlooking the city. Elephant Mountain, about 200 m high, is one of the Four Beasts Mountains, and paths from here go up to higher peaks in Nangang.

listings.name: Tong Hua Night Market
listings.content: This night market caters for the more adventurous eaters. The market featuers not only local foods but dozens of exotic delicacies, including inexpensive Malaysian, Japanese and Taiwanese snacks.
listings.address: Alley 1, Lane 40, Linjiang Street, Da’an District

listings.name: AiYu's Dream Journey Grass Jelly
listings.content: Great Ai Yu Jelly, Grass Jelly, and Tofu Flower desserts. Recommendations: zh-TW 愛玉綜合冰 (ai yu zong he bing);zh-TW 仙草綜合冰(xian cao zong he bing);zh-TW 豆花綜合冰 (dou hua zong he bing -- warning: this contains peanuts, but you can ask for it without them -- "zh-TW 不要花生" (bu yao hua sheng)). Ai Yu is only found in Taiwan.
listings.address: Tonghua Street No. 56 (zh-TW 臺北大安區通化街56zh-TW 號)

listings.name: Kiki Restaurant
listings.content: This restaurant serves authentic Szechwanese peppery hot pot.

listings.name: Mani Mani
listings.content: Innovative vegan meals. Chic and warm environment.

listings.name: Thanh Ky
listings.content: Always busy and popular with Vietnamese expats and locals. Rice noodle soup with spicy beef and curried beef or pork is a specialty.

listings.name: The Pengs' Traditional Hong Kong Cuisine
listings.content: Opened in the 1980s, the food and the decor of the restaurant have not changed since. Known for being more authentically 1980s Hong Kong than most restaurants in Hong Kong today.

listings.name: Yin-Yih Restaurant
listings.content: Dedicated to old style Yangzhou cuisine.

listings.name: Yongkang Beef Noodle
listings.content: One of the top-twenty beef noodle shops in Taipei. Yongkang Beef Noodle occupies the former location of Lao-Zhang Beef Noodle, which is now located next to it.

listings.name: KingSpicy J
listings.content: The infamous restaurant known for its spicy noodle challenge, with rare people able to pass. If you are a fan of spicy foods, you will enjoy their spicy noodle, with four levels and the Challenge level. The third level is considered very spicy in other Taiwanese restaurants. Anyone interested in the Challenge level must have tried the fourth level, then challenge the Challenge level the next day. The restaurant even offers NTD 500 to those who pass, but know your limit before challenging. This is not a joke. Only a hundred people can pass the challenge in 20 years, while more people have been sent to hospitals after challenging.

listings.name: Alleycat's Pizza
listings.content: Generally considered by expats to be the only edible and best traditional Italian pizza in Taipei.

listings.name: Din Tai Fung
listings.content: Famous for its steamed pork dumplings. Worth a detour. Several locations in Taipei and worldwide, but this is the main branch. Gets very crowded even on weekdays so book in advance, or go to other branches such as the one under Taipei 101

listings.name: Niu Ba Ba (688 Beef Bowl)
listings.content: The most expensive beef noodle soup to be had in Taiwan. On average this dish costs N$120. Owner Tony Wong has bowls ranging from a few hundred all the way to $10,000. The simple decor belies the intricate process Wong uses to deliver beef noodles for Taipei's foodies.
listings.address: No. 149, Section 6, Minquan East Road, Neihu District

listings.name: Shinyeh's Table
listings.content: Taiwanese food. Menu has English.

listings.name: Flavors restaurant
listings.content: Located on a back street of busy Renai Rd with a lush garden in front and warm and cozy atmosphere inside. Flavors serves great grilled steaks including rare meat like venison, amazing selection of appetizers in a casual fine dining way.
listings.address: Ren Ai Rd. Sec.4 No.13 Alley 26 Lane 300

listings.name: Jimmy's Kitchen
listings.content: Kobe steak, rib eye, filet mignon, and many other cuts.

listings.name: Pearl Liang
listings.content: Offers unique, fresh, live seafood and dim sum.

listings.name: Peking Do It True
listings.content: This is the place to go if you crave good Beijing cuisine. Visitors may be surprised to see a large photo of former U.S. President George H.W. Bush on the wall, taken when he ate at the restaurant during his trip to Taiwan in 1994.

listings.name: Shang Palace
listings.content: Specialize in Cantonese and regional Chinese cuisines. Dim sum is available for lunch only.

listings.name: San Niu
listings.content: Fresh sashimi and tempura shrimp. Less expensive than most Japanese restaurants of this quality. Clean, comfortable environment.

listings.name: Whalen's
listings.content: Whalen's offer delicious Canadian cuisine such as Poutine and Quiche Lorraine, as well as breakfast omelets and waffles. They also offer a variety of beers. Reservation is recommended since the restaurant is considerably small.
listings.address: No. 145, Section 2, Ānhé Rd, Daan District

listings.name: a.se Cafe
listings.content: Elegant and relaxed interior. Distinctive mismatched furniture. Charcoal gray walls. Warm lighting, Outdoor seating. Excellent coffee. Very friendly and warm service. Dull, elevator music.

listings.name: Cafe Moda Taipei
listings.content: For people who prefer the new concept of a boutique cafe, the specialty of this place by far are the 100% Organic Guatemalan quality coffee beverages they offer in a cozy ambient mixed with art fashion and great music. A small but fancy terrace is perfect for enjoying beverages on a fresh day. They also have imported beer, wine, tea, juices and other snacks in their menu, including cheese and Italian fruit cake. They have a multicultural staff fluent in Chinese, English, and Spanish (German and Japanese depending on the day you go), so feel relaxed if Chinese is not your mother tongue as this place is geared for expats and locals that prefer a stronger kind of gourmet organic coffee.
listings.price: Coffee beverages between NT$120 and NT$200
listings.address: 1F, No 11, Lane 49, Sec 1, Anhe Road, Daan District

listings.name: Minimal Cafe
listings.content: This cafe is famous for having many resident cats living inside of it (49, according to the wait staff). In fact, the owner of this cafe loves cats so much, stray ones are adopted, spayed/neutered, then allowed to live in the cafe. Thus, as you drink your beverage, don't be surprised if cats are checking you out. This cafe is indeed clean despite all the cats, and has tasty mid-range priced desserts and coffee, as well as salads/meals. The cats are friendly, if not always looking for a warm lap to sleep on. The younger cats might jump from lap to lap, just to find a playmate, even if the wiser, older cats do not care for such shenanigans.
listings.address: 106zh-TW 台北市Taipeizh-TW 泰順街2zh-TW 巷 Tai4Shun4 Jie1 Lane 2, #42, Daan District

listings.name: Martinez Coffee
listings.content: A coffee shop and supplier of high quality coffee. Elegant and relaxing interior. Outdoor seating. Cakes and dessert

listings.name: Out of Office Coffee Roastery
listings.content: A Zen minimalist cafe. Spacious. Great coffee. Cakes and snacks

listings.name: Saturn Landing Turkish Coffee
listings.content: Spacious and light. Outdoor seating at the rear. Excellent Turkish coffee, along with standard coffees. Healthy meals. Turkish interior design and background music.

listings.name: Carnegies
listings.content: With an outdoor patio, it's perfect for those who prefer a quieter and less smoky atmosphere. The scene is geared toward the 30+ expats and locals.

listings.name: Club Myst
listings.content: One of the hottest night club in Taipei. Often cited as having the best view of the Taipei 101 building. Large and active dance floor. Open all nights, Wednesday night is ladies night with free entry.
listings.address: No. 12, 9F, ATT4FUN Building, Song Shou Rd, Xinyi Dist

listings.name: Elektro
listings.content: Another large and popular nightclub, previously was called Spark but was closed down due to some police controversy.
listings.address: 6F, ATT4FUN Building, Song Shou Rd, Xinyi Dist

listings.name: Fourplay Cuisine
listings.content: A quiet bar/restaurant with creative drinks. Your shot may include a helium balloon, a water pipe, fire or dry ice.

listings.name: Luxy
listings.content: One of the most well-known clubs in Taipei. Luxy has two levels: the lower level has a side room playing house/techno and a main room playing hip-hop; the upper level is a lounge with a small dance floor overlooking the main room. Cover charge goes up after 23:00. Get there early to avoid a line.
listings.address: 5F, 201 Zhongxiao E. Rd Section 4, Daan District

listings.name: Ziga Zaga
listings.content: This club specializes in cocktails and Italian cuisine - both the service and food are excellent. It's popular with locals and expats. Ladies Night is on Wednesday nights.
listings.address: No.2, Song Shou Road Grand Hyatt Taipei

listings.name: Stop By Teahouse
listings.content: A tea cafe in a modern setting, offering a full range of brewing options. Ask to see the private tearoom in the basement.

listings.name: Teng
listings.content: A rustic tea house and art studio in the heart of Taipei.

listings.name: Wistaria House
listings.content: Wistaria is set in a traditional house, complete with tatami mats, and is a great place to spend an afternoon relaxing with friends and soaking up the atmosphere of Taiwan.

listings.name: Happy Fruit Juice Bar
listings.content: Happy Fruit Juice Bar is a fresh fruit juice bar decorated with a Greek cafe interior. The store is family owned and run by a mom and four sisters. They serve tea, fresh fruit juice, milk pearl tea and other drinks. It's a great place to grab something cool and refreshing on a hot day. Also, Happy Fruit Juice bar's right beside the Mofo burger joint, so it's a perfect place to get a healthy drink to wash down that burger afterwards, or to simply sit down at after a trek through Yongkang St!

listings.name: KDM Hotel
listings.content: Decent, standard budget hotel without trimmings, but in a desired location, near all the commercial businesses and entertainment avenues.
listings.address: No.8, Sec. 3, Jhongsiao E. Rd., Da-an District

listings.name: Les Suites Daan Taipei
listings.content: Calming ambiance is felt throughout this hotel, with soft lighting and muted colour palette adding to the mood. Staff are helpful and professional, and a complimemtary afternoon tea is served downstairs in the internet terminals, making it a perfect stay for the business traveller.

listings.name: Royal Best Suites
listings.content: Spacious and comfortable rooms decorated in a Victorian style decor.

listings.name: Taipei Fullerton Fu-Xing South
listings.content: Tastefully decorated and geared toward business travelers. Very polite and attentive staff. Free wifi in the lobby only, not in the rooms (but rooms do have ethernet ports and cables for laptops, and there is a good business center in the lobby). Surrounded by restaurants and convenience stores.

listings.name: Le Méridien Taipei
listings.content: One of Taipei's newest international hotels.

listings.name: Grand Hyatt Taipei
listings.content: Next to Taipei 101 and Taipei World Trade Center, at the very heart of the New Taipei, a burgeoning business, shopping and entertainment district. Stunning, top end hotel with sleek and modern furnishings. Room service is prompt and delicious.

listings.name: Howard Plaza Hotel
listings.content: Centrally located and convenient for MRT. Rooms are spacious with walk in closets and fresh fruit and water is provided for daily. Internet access is fast and free.

listings.name: Shangri-La Far Eastern Plaza Hotel
listings.content: Asian-inspired interior design that impresses with the attention to detail. 5-star hotel.

listings.name: W Taipei
listings.content: Opened in 2011.

listings.name: Grand Hotel
listings.content: This majestic hotel has graced the photograph albums of numerous generations of Taipei tourists. And, although the increase in other attractions may have led to it losing its status as the must-see-destination, this imposing structure, built in the style of a Beijing palace, still manages to attract bus loads of tourists wishing to have their photograph taken outside the main building and in the foyer. The tea rooms on the first floor are a good place to relax and absorb the grandeur of dynastic China. The hills behind the hotel are crisscrossed by a vast network of trails, footpaths, pavilions, and an abandoned military anti-aircraft base and are a popular exercise spot for locals and urban explorers. Getting there: MRT to Yuanshan station, then hop on the free shuttle bus.

listings.name: Martyr's Shrine
listings.content: temple memorializing those who gave their lives for the Republic of China (ROC) during its tenure on mainland China and it's later existence on Taiwan. A changing of the guard ceremony is performed at the top of the hour where a military honor guard performs an impressive series of gun twirling and tossing in front of astounded tourists. To get to the shrine take the MRT to the Jiantan Station, then take the Red 3 bus from the same side of the street the rest of the way, get off at the third stop.

listings.name: Xingtian Temple
listings.content: The temple was built in 1967 and was devoted to Guangong (AD 162-219), a famous deified general who lived during the Three Kingdoms period, and he is an important character in the Chinese classic Romance of the Three Kingdoms. The temple forbids the killing of animals as an offering, so you will see offerings of only fresh flowers, fruits and tea on the main altar. Many believers feel that this is a very efficacious temple, and it is frequently thronged with people praying for help and seeking divine guidance by consulting oracle blocks. Outside the temple, the underground pedestrian passages under the Minquan - Songjiang intersection are filled with fortune-tellers and vendors who take commercial advantage of the temple's popularity.
listings.address: Corner of Minquan East Road and Songjiang Road

listings.name: Taipei Cultural Mosque
listings.content: The third mosque built in Taiwan.
listings.address: No. 3, Lane 25, Sec. 1, Xinhai Road, Zhongzheng District

listings.name: Miniatures Museum of Taiwan
listings.content: This is a small, private museum that is a monument to a patient and steady hand. The 40 bulb chandelier, which is the size of grain of rice, is one of the many impressive pieces on display. The museum is in the same building as Thai Airways.
listings.price: Adults NT$250, concessions NT$200, children NT$150, Concessions-Elderly NT$125

listings.name: Su Ho Memorial Paper Museum
listings.content: This museum was founded by Su Ho Chen, one of Taiwan's last few masters of papermaking, and who was killed in 1990 in a plane crash. You can enjoy exhibits about paper, and make your own sheet of paper here.

listings.name: Taipei Fine Arts Museum
listings.content: The museum displays work of local and international artists.
listings.price: Adult admission NT$30, concessions and residents of Taipei NT$15, groups (+20 people) NT$21. Sa 17:00-20:30 free admission (students all day)

listings.name: Taipei Story House
listings.content: On the same plot of land as the Taipei Fine Arts Museum, this tea merchant's 19th-century European style house has been converted into a gallery and museum space with visiting exhibitions and the occasional traditional music concert. The patio serves as a tea garden, which offers pleasant views over the Danshui River and beyond.

listings.name: Dajia Riverside Park
listings.content: This park is a 12-km-long green belt on the south bank of the Keelung River. One of the beautiful banks in Taipei. Basketball, tennis, and badminton courts are available, as are bicycles for rent.

listings.name: Zhongshan Fine Arts Park
listings.content: This park is south of the Taipei Fine Arts Museum. The open green space and many stabiles are on display in the park.

listings.name: Songshan Cultural and Creative Park
listings.content: A park with various galleries and small museums such as the Taiwan Design Museum, centered around a former tobacco factory turned arts and crafts mall with boutique Eslite shops. Tax refund is available with a 20% fee.

listings.name: Children's Recreation Center
listings.content: It is an amusement park on Zhongshan North Road Sec. 3, nearest MRT station is 'Yuanshan' on Danshui Line. The center was created by city government in 1991. It has old-fashioned rides, folk art museum, IMAX theater and more. This place is great for younger kids.

listings.name: Miramar Entertainment Park
listings.content: This up-scale shopping mall in the suburb of Dazhi operates a large Ferris wheel that offers great views over the city. It is especially spectacular at night, when not only the city but also the Ferris wheel is illuminated. The 15-minute ride costs NT$150 on weekdays and NT$200 on weekends. The same complex also houses a 3D Imax movie theater and a multi-screen Warner Village cinema.
listings.price: NT$150 on weekdays and NT$200 on weekends

listings.name: Spot - Taipei Film House
listings.content: The former residence of the U.S. Ambassador has been transformed into an art center that focuses on independent films. In addition to screenings, the house also has great cafes and restaurants that spill out onto balconies and into the garden. The bookstore offers a good selection of hard-to-get art/independent films on DVD, though for other movies, prices are lower at regular DVD rental stores.

listings.name: TaipeiEYE
listings.content: The venue is recognized for its traditional Chinese and Taiwanese performing arts. Following a tradition that dates back to the 18th century. The 90-minute evening show is a form of Chinese opera that incorporates mime, dance, acrobatics and martial arts. During the live performance, the dialogue and even the songs are translated into multiple languages, including English.

listings.name: Shijie Vegetarian Restaurant
listings.content: A very traditional family run Chinese vegetarian restaurant. Amazing food. Very little English spoken, but photographs of dishes on menu.
listings.address: No 9, Alley 6, Lane 40, Changan West Road

listings.name: Addiction Aquatic Development
listings.content: If you are craving fresh and super affordable seafood, sashimi and sushi, this fish market is the place to indulge. Includes ten different foodie areas, including an outdoor grill joint, sushi bar, and gourmet grocery.
listings.address: No. 18, Alley 2, Lane 410, Minzu East Road

listings.name: Blossom Rena Vegan Cafe
listings.content: Innovative vegan cuisine. Natural, minimalistic decor. Helpful and fast service.
listings.address: No. 26-1, Section 3, Zhongshan N Rd, Zhongshan District

listings.name: Thai Star
listings.content: Shrimp Toast, Beef Stew, Chicken, Papaya Salad are most famous dishes!

listings.name: Tien Hsiang Lo
listings.content: Authentic Hangzhou cuisine. Reservations are recommended.

listings.name: Ching-Yeh Aoba
listings.content: The most famous Taiwanese restaurant in Taipei, beside the Zhongshan North Road.

listings.name: Mitsui Japanese Cuisine
listings.content: The best Japanese cuisine in Taipei.

listings.name: Shabu Sen
listings.content: This place serves great Japanese/Taiwanese style hot pot dishes. It is a family run restaurant. The environment is clean and refreshing. The owner Ms. Chiu hand picks her ingredients daily from the market. Try the Kobe beef pot and mushroom pot. The price is very reasonable with well selected ingredients. English menu available.

listings.name: Ruth's Chris Steak House
listings.content: Perhaps Taipei's best-known and best American steakhouse.

listings.name: Wang Steak House
listings.content: An upscale chain steakhouse known for its signature "Wang steak".

listings.name: GaBee
listings.content: Probably the best cafe in Taipei for coffee lovers. Winner of the 2008 Barista championships, they take coffee and latte art very seriously. The waffles are excellent too.
listings.address: No 21, Minsheng East Road, Section 3, Alley 113

listings.name: Libo Cafe
listings.content: A rustic and cool cafe. Excellent coffee and cakes. Fast and friendly service.

listings.name: Recall Cafe
listings.content: A pleasant cafe offering standard cafe food, desserts and coffee. Friendly and helpful staff.
listings.address: No 34, Lane 42 Zhongshan North Road, Sec 2

listings.name: Wooden Sounds and Garnet Cru
listings.content: Excellent no-nonsense coffee. Warm ambiance and distinctive decor set to electronic music. Simple, straightforward cakes available, but no meals. Good selection of teas.

listings.name: Standing Room
listings.content: It is the standing style bar and restaurant with a traditional Japanese hors d'oeuvres, with world wide classic beverages. Its perfect location to have the quick dinner and drink for a busy business person. "Happy Hour" everyday open-20:30.

listings.name: My Place Bar & Restaurant
listings.content: Still going strong after 30 plus years. Serves great food, has two bars, pool table, and shows live sports on multiple screens. There is outside seating for smokers. One of the premier bars in Taipei for watching the upcoming World Cup. Happy Hour selected beers $100, special draught beer $100 all night.

listings.name: The Brass Monkey
listings.content: Great atmosphere with live sports shown on big screens. There’s always something going on - it’s never a regular night. Friendly staffs are ready to serve you with good food and a wide selection of drinks. Go have a dance on their famous Thursday ladies nights.

listings.name: Donghwa Hotel
listings.content: Good value hotel that provides guests with a warm and homey experience.

listings.name: Happy Family Hostel 1 & 2
listings.content: Happy Family is an old favorite in the city and it's managed by the very friendly and helpful John Lee.
listings.price: Dorm: NT$400, Single: NT$700, Cheaper rates are available for long term stays

listings.name: Homey Hostel
listings.content: A clean and modern hostel. Friendly and enthusiatic staff. Free wifi. Free breakfast.
listings.address: 7F, No. 180, Changan West Road, Zhongshan District

listings.name: Jiantan Overseas Youth Activity Center
listings.content: A pleasant HI-accredited hostel with gardens and the best view of the Grand Hotel in town, also convenient for Shilin Night Market and the Fine Arts Museum (both within walking distance) and the National Palace Museum (a 15 minute journey by taxi/bus). Coin laundry, Internet access, convenience store on site. The facility is primarily a youth activity center catering to groups, so it is often full during school vacations and at weekends — book ahead.
listings.price: Twin room: NT$2,200-2,500, Double room: NT$3,200, Six single beds: NT$4,500
listings.address: 16 Zhongshan North Road, Sec.4, Zhongshan District

listings.name: Travel Talk Taipei Backpackers
listings.content: The international airport bus stop & city bus stop is just right in front of the hostel. There are famous temple (Hsing Tien Kung), traditional morning market, local food shops, future teller shops and foot massage & spa stores around.
listings.address: 2F, No.96, Sec.2, Minquan E. Rd., Taipei city

listings.name: Check Inn
listings.content: A minimalist and chic hotel in the centre of Taipei. 24 hour reception. Cafe.

listings.name: First Hotel
listings.content: Ten-story hotel that has received mixed reviews due to the poor customer service and somewhat shabby rooms.

listings.name: Hotel B
listings.content: Cozy and well equipped hotel at a reasonable price, located at the heart of Taipei. Renovated in 2009 with brand new rooms and friendlier services.

listings.name: Les Suites Ching-Cheng Hotel
listings.content: A small and very comfortable hotel. Excellent service - the manager is very kind and will help you find good local restaurants and places to visit.

listings.name: The Leofoo Hotel
listings.content: Aging, although solid choice for those on a budget with clean and comfortable rooms.

listings.name: The Riviera Hotel
listings.content: The Riviera Taipei hotel is a boutique hotel adjacent to Taipei Expo Centre

listings.name: Grand Victoria Hotel
listings.content: Near the Miramar Entertainment Park.

listings.name: Regent Taipei
listings.content: Sophisticated top end hotel that displays elegance throughout its rooms and building. Large rooms, helpful staff and wonderful amenities.
listings.address: No 3, Lane 39, Section 2, Zhongshan North Road

listings.name: The Landis
listings.content: One of the city's most luxurious hotels, the Ritz has a comfortable sophistication that everyone can enjoy. Each of their 100 rooms is equipped with the most modern technology like temperature and humidity control, phones with dataports for fax or modems and voice mail service and cable TV. Guests can also dine in two of the most famous restaurants in the city at their hotel, the Tien Hsiang Lo and Paris 1930, both serving fresh, tasty cuisine.

listings.name: Hotel Metropolitan Premier Taipei
listings.content: Great for business travellers, this 5-star hotel is well equipped for business functions with expansive meeting space and a business center offering secretarial support and translations. Eight restaurants and a hotel piano bar are the perfect way to unwind after a day of busy meetings.

listings.name: National Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
listings.content: The memorial hall is a famous but controversial symbol of both Taipei and the Republic of China, as expected of its namesake. Every morning, at 06:00 in the summer and 06:30 in the winter, the nation's flag is raised in the square in front of the memorial. The huge courtyard serves as a place for both national celebrations as well as a platform to voice one's disapproval of the government. The memorial consists of a large bronze statue of Chiang Kai-shek, watched over by two motionless honor guards who are replaced every hour in a rifle twirling ceremony. Downstairs, there is a museum. One exhibit is of Chiang's life, complete with his cars and uniforms. The other exhibit is on life under Chiang's rule, focusing on martial law and the suppression of speech and political opposition. Even if you are not into memorials, the gardens, with their Chinese-style ponds, are definitely worth a visit. The grounds of the memorial are also a favorite place for locals to gather and practice martial arts, though you'll have to be there early if you want to see this. Most people begin their work-out at around sunrise, and will have left for the office before 08:00.

listings.name: National Museum Of History
listings.content: This museum is in Taipei Botanical Garden, and is famous for its varied selection of exhibits, including Tang dynasty tri-color pottery and Shang dynasty bronzes.

listings.name: National Taiwan Museum
listings.content: This museum is in 'Peace Park' (near Taipei Main Station) in a splendid Baroque and Renaissance style building. Opened in 1899, it was Taiwan's first museum and focuses on anthropology and the fauna and flora of the island.

listings.name: 228 Memorial Museum
listings.content: Commemorates the 228 incident that occurred on February 28, 1947, in which locals revolting against Chinese rule were brutally massacred by the Kuomintang. This incident continues to be a key impetus behind the Taiwan independence movement to this day.

listings.name: National Taiwan University
listings.content: Taiwan's pre-eminent institution of higher education. The campus grounds are surrounded by several blocks of shops, bookshops, cafes and tea houses popular with students and scholars. Browse through the stalls and booths directly across the street from the main entrance of the university (don't forget there is a lot more just behind the main street), grab a bite or two of the popular snacks, such as fresh fruit, spice-cooked meats, soy goodies, sky-high ice cream cones, sweets, shaved ice, tapioca teas or fresh bread. You can also sample the yummy Taiwanese fried chicken chain Ding Gua Gua. Try a "Gua Gua Bao," a flavorful sticky rice pouch. There are many American fast food restaurants across the street on the right of the University, right next to several wonderful bookshops.

listings.name: Presidential Office Building
listings.content: It was built during the Japanese colonial period as the residence of the Governor-General of Taiwan. It is now the official workplace of the President of the Republic of China. Public access is generally restricted to specific open house days which are published on the web-site.

listings.name: Qidong Street Japanese Houses
listings.content: A street of well-preserved Japanese-style wooden houses which date back to various periods during and before the Japanese colonial periods.

listings.name: Sun Yun-suan Memorial Museum
listings.content: The museum displays permanent exhibitions of handwritten diaries, manuscripts, photographs and personal items of the ROC's former Premier Sun Yun-suan.
listings.address: No. 10, Lane 6, Section 2, Chongqing South Road

listings.name: Museum of Drinking Water
listings.content: The Museum of Drinking Water was completed in 1908, and is the first pumping station and filtration plant in Taipei. The museum is in the Taipei Water Park.

listings.name: National Taiwan Arts Education Center
listings.content: Formal Kenkō Jinja (Chienkung Shrine), whose architecture is a mixture of Chinese (such as three-gated torii), Japanese, and Western (such as dome-shaped roof) elements. After World War II, it was renovated to National Central Library. Now it is repurposed to serve as National Arts Education Center and there are two theaters (one indoor and one outdoor) and three exhibition rooms.

listings.name: 228 Peace Memorial Park
listings.content: This park is on the north side of Katagalan Boulevard and the MRT station 'National Taiwan University Hospital' on the Danshui line. The park was founded by the Japanese in 1907 as New Park (新公園). The name was changed in 1996 to commemorate those killed in the 228 Incident of 28 February 1947, in which locals revolting against Chinese rule were brutally massacred by the ruling Kuomintang under Chiang Kai-shek. The park is popular with practitioners of taichi and senior citizens playing Chinese chess. The National Taiwan Museum marks the northern entrance to the park.

listings.name: Taipei Botanical Garden
listings.content: This beautiful garden has inspired the citizens of Taipei for over one hundred years. The lotus ponds are a hallmark of the park and are especially captivating when these symbols of peace are in full bloom and swaying in the summer breeze. The gardens are close to the National Museum of History.

listings.name: Huashan 1914 Creative Park
listings.content: What is now Huashan 1914 Creative Park opened in 1916 as Taihoku Winery during Japanese rule. It was privately owned winery that produced sake and ginseng wines, and bred moth orchids. The park as it is now was opened in 2005 and features a number of facilities for public use.

listings.name: Yixian Park
listings.content: An area of parkland that contains the Dr. Sun Yat-sen Memorial House.

listings.name: Hua Shan Cultural and Creative Industry Center
listings.content: This former brewery has been transformed into a creative space in a park. The exhibitions are well presented and imaginative and the theater performances, while less formal than those at the National Theater, are first rate. The center also has a number of cool cafes - some with outdoor seating - an art movie theater and a number of shops selling innovative crafts.

listings.name: Taipei Artist Village
listings.content: This village provides residency programs for Taiwanese artists and others from around the world. They provide gallery and studio space for artists. They also have a few cafes which are excellent for a mid-day break while exploring Taipei.
listings.price: You are free to roam around the village

listings.name: Treasure Hill Artist Village
listings.content: Another artist village.
listings.address: No. 2, Alley 14, Ln. 230 Dingzhou Rd. Sec. 3

listings.name: Zhongshan Hall
listings.content: The buildings were completed in the period of Japanese rule on December 26, 1936. In 1945, The former Taipei City Hall was renamed as Zhongshan Hall. In 1992, the building has been identified to Second monuments of the country. Later it was assigned as a cultural space that hosts cultural and art events.

listings.name: National Theater Hall and National Concert Hall
listings.content: Located in the grounds of the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial, it is an excellent place to see performances of a Taiwanese play or a dance troupe. They also host many international events. Taiwan's National Symphony Orchestra performs at the National Concert Hall. The building's neo-classic Chinese architecture is especially stunning when flood-lit at night.

listings.name: Taipei Water Park
listings.content: The park is built around the Museum of Drinking Water, housed in the former pumping station building and showcasing some of the machinery used to provide water to the city. Many facilities are all about water. The most popular are water slides and swimming spas. But the facilities are open only in summer (entry included with the museum ticket)

listings.name: Happy Farm Vegetarian Restaurant
listings.content: Offers simple and tasty Chinese buffet style vegetarian meals.
listings.address: 2F, No 16, Lane 683, Roosevelt Road, Sec 3, Gongguang

listings.name: Su De Su Shi
listings.content: A buffet style restaurant offering a wide range of Chinese vegetarian dishes.
listings.address: No 21, Lane 283, Roosevelt Road, Sec 3, Gongguan

listings.name: Thai Guo Xiao Guan
listings.content: This small Thai restaurant is in Gongguan.

listings.name: Three Idiots Toast and Curry
listings.content: Indian chefs offering interesting fusion dishes.
listings.address: No 28, Lane 263, Roosevelt Road, Sec 3, Gongguan

listings.name: Mary Jane's Pizza
listings.content: No. Taipei (near Taida). Great thin crust pizza at reasonable prices, they also do delivery.

listings.name: Among Cafe
listings.content: A cafe with an alternative vibe. Excellent coffee served in distinctive clay cups. Alternative music. Warm lighting. Excellent selection of books. Healthy and freshly cooked food options. Cool and laid back owner and staff.

listings.name: Aura Cafe
listings.content: A chic and stylish cafe. Excellent coffee, including drip. Friendly and helpful service.
listings.address: No9, Lane 269, Roosevelt Road, Sec 3, Gongguan.

listings.name: Coffee Lab
listings.content: This small coffee shop roasts their own beans on site. 3 resident cats keep patrons company as they sip carefully crafted lattes.
listings.address: No. 6, Lane 64, Section 2, Zhōngxiào East Road

listings.name: Notch Cafe
listings.content: A two storey cafe with a backstreet vibe. Excellent coffee. Innovative light meals and snacks.

listings.name: Trilobite Cafe
listings.content: Serves excellent coffees offering a wide selection of espresso. The two resident dogs are very friendly too.

listings.name: Taipei Brewery
listings.content: A godsend for the thirsty budget traveler in a city of pricey bars, this is most certainly the cheapest bar in town. This is a great place to find the rare Taiwan Draft Beer, which has a 2-week expiration and usually can only be found in a few restaurants and stores in the same city as the brewery. It's attached to the brewery where Taiwan Beer is made, close to the intersection of Bade and Jianguo Roads. The restaurant is located in an inconspicuous warehouse deep inside the brewery entrance. What it lacks in ambiance it more than makes up for in value. The draft beer 500 ml is NT$60, but you might want to opt for a bottled 600 ml malt beer for NT$55. Interior and exterior seating are available.

listings.name: The Wall Live House
listings.content: The biggest venue for independent live music - Taiwanese bands playing everything from rock to reggae.

listings.name: Revolver
listings.content: Just across the road from the monument to Chiang Kai Shek, this is a bar on the ground floor and a live music venue on the second floor. The indoors part is often full and partrons will stand outside chatting. This bar also has Taiwan Beer Gold Label on tap.

listings.name: Eight Elephants & Dreaming Dragon
listings.content: Rated best hostel in Taiwan for 2010 by HostelWorld.com. A very clean and stylish hostel. Helpful info for travelers and job-seekers.

listings.name: Camels' Oasis Hostel
listings.content: Cheap but decent, clean hostel in a good location, only 5 mins walk from MRT C.K.S. memorial hall station.
listings.address: 2F.-1, No.78, Ningbo W. St., Taipei city

listings.name: Taipei Hostel
listings.content: Well-known for its numerous facilities, helpful staff, and excellent rates. Ideal location near the MRT station and several restaurants.
listings.price: Dorm: NT$300 (NT$1500/week). Single bed room: NT$500 (NT$2500/week)

listings.name: World Scholar House
listings.content: A clean hostel. Dorm and private rooms available, with the rates running NT$350-NT$500.

listings.name: Taipei Key Mall Traveler Hostel
listings.content: This hostel is opposite the Taipei Main Station on the 15th floor of the building where the K-Mall is located, next to the tall Mitsukoshi building.
listings.price: NT$490 per night per person and includes breakfast, NT$250 for children under 12

listings.name: See You Hotel
listings.content: Modern, clean and well appointed, with features such as flat screen tvs and air conditioning in rooms, as well as spacious bathrooms. Staff are very friendly.

listings.name: New Mayflower Hotel
listings.content: Large and comfortable rooms and with modern amenities.

listings.name: Guest House Taiwanmex
listings.content: Air-con 2-bed dorms, single and double rooms. Free Wi-Fi, free laundry.

listings.name: Cosmos Hotel
listings.content: In front of Taipei Main Station. The dated decor brings down the tone in this otherwise comfortable hotel. Service standard in the hotel was good with staff being responsive but not very knowledgeable.

listings.name: Hotel Flowers
listings.content: Decent value for money, take note that the rooms are extremely small.

listings.name: YMCA
listings.content: English speaking staff is friendly. Has in house restaurant. Rooms on the street side have a balcony.

listings.name: Caesar Park Taipei
listings.content: Walking distance to the Presidential Palace, the hotels location is its biggest drawcard. Rooms are rather soul less and the breakfast buffet is standard, though edible.

listings.name: Sheraton Grand Taipei Hotel
listings.content: An older hotel in an area isolated from shops and other amenities. However, it offers a high overall standard in the rooms and the service.
